---
title: "Computational competencies"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ghedata)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

In June 2025 the members of the group answered a survey on their computational competencies. The table `computational` holds the answers as counts: one row per question and answer, with the number of respondents who gave it. It holds no row per respondent, so the answers to two questions cannot be combined.

`r unique(computational$respondents)` people answered the survey.

## Experience with Git and GitHub

```{r}
computational |>
  filter(question %in% c("experience_git", "experience_github")) |>
  select(question, answer, n) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Tools used

Three questions allowed several picks. Their rows count the respondents per pick and do not add up to the number of respondents.

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of the development environments the respondents have used, by number of respondents."
#| fig-height: 4
computational |>
  filter(question == "ides_used") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(answer, n))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Respondents", y = NULL, title = "Development environments used") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of the AI tools the respondents have used, by number of respondents."
#| fig-height: 6
computational |>
  filter(question == "llm_tools_used") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(answer, n))) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Respondents", y = NULL, title = "AI tools used") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
computational |>
  filter(question == "other_languages") |>
  select(language = answer, respondents = n) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
